title: Audit Log Explorer: advanced search, pagination and export with saved-query support
creator: Marco Leung
description: Build an Audit Log Explorer in the Console that lets operators and auditors search, filter, paginate, and export audit events (CSV/JSON). Support saved queries and ensure RBAC v2 enforces view/export permissions. Exports must be secure, performant, and traceable for compliance audits.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI with time-range, actor, action, resource-type, resource-id, and metadata free-text filters
Server-side cursor-based pagination (opaque cursor) with stable sort by event_timestamp DESC
Export button that streams results to CSV or JSON; for result sets > 100k events use background export job with download link
Saved queries persisted per-org and sharable via immutable link; saved queries respect RBAC at access time
Export and view actions are recorded to the audit log (who exported what and when)
API endpoint /api/v1/audit/search supporting same filters and export formats with API key auth
Performance: initial search response < 400ms for last-24h index-backed queries; export job submission < 200ms
Security: only users with audit.viewer or audit.admin role (RBAC v2) can view or export events; exports require additional confirmation for PII-likely fields
notes_decisions: Decided to use cursor-based pagination rather than offset to avoid inconsistency on live event streams
Will implement export streaming for <=100k rows and background job (S3 presigned download) for larger exports
Saved queries stored encrypted at rest, indexed by org_id and creator_id; sharing implemented with ACL entries that point to RBAC groups
UI will show estimated row count and warn if export contains high-PII risk fields (based on metadata tags)
Audit exports themselves will create an audit event with export metadata (filters, format, initiated_by)
To avoid expensive wide scans, restrict free-text wildcard searches to last 90 days unless user confirms broader range

deploy_plan: 1) Backend API and DB schema migrations behind feature flag. 2) UI behind FF with RBAC gating. 3) Enable streaming exports for small datasets. 4) Flip to background job path for large datasets. 5) Gradual rollout: orgs with 'early-access' flag first, monitor export job durations and error rates.
risks: Large exports causing high memory/IO on index nodes -> mitigated by background job + incremental export workers
Potential PII exposure in CSV if filters are too broad -> mitigate with warning/confirmation and PII-tagged column scrubbing rules
RBAC mis-evaluation could leak cross-org saved queries -> require security review and automated unit tests for ACL checks
Export download links must expire and be logged to satisfy compliance requests
